claims.text: Key takeaway and body: deductible is what you pay for covered services before the plan starts to pay; $2,000 example
claims.quote: The amount you pay for covered health care services before your insurance plan starts to pay. With a $2,000 deductible, for example, you pay the first $2,000 of covered services yourself.

claims.text: Deductible section (rewritten): Marketplace plans pay full cost of certain preventive benefits before the deductible; many plans pay for some services like a checkup before it is met (also FAQ deductible vs coinsurance, FAQ deductible vs copay)
claims.quote: Many plans pay for certain services, like a checkup or disease management programs, before you've met your deductible. ... All Marketplace health plans pay the full cost of certain preventive benefits even before you meet your deductible.

claims.text: Takeaway and stacking step 2: after the deductible you usually pay a copay or coinsurance while the insurer pays the rest
claims.quote: After you pay your deductible, you usually pay only a copayment or coinsurance for covered services. Your insurance company pays the rest.

claims.text: Premium tradeoff (rewritten): lower-premium plans generally have higher deductibles; higher-premium plans lower deductibles
claims.quote: Generally, plans with lower monthly premiums have higher deductibles. Plans with higher monthly premiums usually have lower deductibles.

claims.text: FAQ premium vs copay: premium is the monthly amount for coverage whether or not you get services; a copay is a fixed amount for a covered service
claims.quote: A monthly amount you pay for coverage whether you get services or not.

claims.text: Takeaway and copay section (rewritten): copay is a fixed amount for a covered service, like $20 for a doctor visit
claims.quote: A fixed amount ($20, for example) you pay for a covered health care service after you've paid your deductible.

claims.text: Copay section and FAQs (rewritten): HealthCare.gov's definition describes the copay as paid after the deductible; before that you pay the full allowed amount; copay continues after deductible
claims.quote: If you've paid your deductible : You pay $20, usually at the time of the visit. If you haven't met your deductible: You pay $100, the full allowable amount for the visit.

claims.text: Premium tradeoff (rewritten): lower-premium plans generally have higher copayments
claims.quote: Generally plans with lower monthly premiums have higher copayments. Plans with higher monthly premiums usually have lower copayments.

claims.text: Takeaway, coinsurance section and FAQs: coinsurance is the percentage of a covered service (like 20%) you pay after the deductible
claims.quote: The percentage of costs of a covered health care service you pay (20%, for example) after you've paid your deductible.

claims.text: Stacking step 1: before the deductible is met you pay the full allowed amount
claims.quote: If you haven't met your deductible: You pay the full allowed amount, $100.

claims.text: Worked example: $3,000 deductible, 20% coinsurance, $12,000 of covered care; 20% of remaining $9,000 is $1,800
claims.quote: Allowable costs are $12,000. Deductible: $3,000 Coinsurance: 20% Out-of-pocket maximum: $6,850 You'd pay all of the first $3,000 (your deductible). You'll pay 20% of the remaining $9,000, or $1,800 (your coinsurance).

claims.text: Worked example: total $4,800, below the example plan's $6,850 out-of-pocket maximum
claims.quote: So your total out-of-pocket costs would be $4,800

claims.text: Premium tradeoff (rewritten): lower-premium plans generally have higher coinsurance
claims.quote: Generally speaking, plans with low monthly premiums have higher coinsurance, and plans with higher monthly premiums have lower coinsurance.

claims.text: Takeaway and deductible section: 2025 average deductible for single coverage with a general annual deductible is $1,886
claims.quote: The average deductible amount in 2025 for workers with single coverage and a general annual deductible is $1,886, similar to last year.

claims.text: Deductible section: 88% of single-coverage workers have a general annual deductible that must be met before most services are paid for
claims.quote: Eighty-eight percent of workers with single coverage have a general annual deductible that must be met before most services are paid for by the plan

claims.text: Copay section (new): most covered workers with a deductible in HMO, PPO and POS plans did not have to meet it before primary care office visits were covered; FAQ deductible vs copay
claims.quote: large shares (69% in HMOs, 78% in PPOs, 57% in POS plans, and 66% in HDHP/HRAs) are enrolled in plans where the deductible does not have to be met before physician office visits for primary care are covered

claims.text: Copay section (new): HSA-qualified HDHPs generally pay only for preventive services before the deductible
claims.quote: HSA-qualified plans generally only pay for preventive services before the deductible is met.

claims.text: FAQ copay and coinsurance at once (new): 8% of covered workers had both a copayment and coinsurance for a hospital admission
claims.quote: When admitted to the hospital, 65% of covered workers have coinsurance requirements, 11% have a copayment, and 8% have both a copayment and coinsurance requirement.
